verdict.rationale: Bento's own marketing claims that every prompt, skill, and model change is versioned, diffable, and reversible. Its automation-like fixes (skills, subagents, tools, nudges) also go through a shadow-mode, candidate-to-promote review before reaching full traffic. However, this rests on one headline claim with no documented workflow for viewing history, reviewing diffs, or executing a rollback. It is also unclear whether alert rules and signals are covered. missing for 10: documented versioning/diff/rollback mechanics (UI, CLI, or API), coverage of signals and alert rules, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Every prompt, skill, and model change is versioned, diffable, and reversible. Trace any regression back to the change that caused it.
Reusable, trigger-based fixes: skills, subagents, and tools that graduate from candidate to promote as they prove themselves in production.
The nudge ships in shadow mode, is scored against the outcome it was meant to fix, and graduates to 100% traffic only if it provably helps.
